DISCOVERED

Nobody asked for these. The prover runs every probe in the catalogue into one store, closes it under the same rules the handmade theorems use, and this is everything it reached - the goal was never named, so no conclusion here can have been aimed at. What is left is judging them, which is why the seven scores are on every row and the weighting is a set of sliders rather than a number somebody chose for you. 4 theories over 4 lattices and 2 regimes, 120 ticks.

fatal fraction = pair leaves nothingpair states
premise survival/what-kills-a-carrier
how often a meeting is fatal is how many of the states a facing pair can be in leave nothing at all, over how many states there are - both counted exhaustively by applying the rule to a real pair. Nothing is sampled and no run length can change either count

by a ratio of counts

the derivation, 53 steps
Fgrel = Fg · retardation · γmr-ms
premise definition:gravity.relativistic
so the force is the one between bodies at rest, times what retardation does to what arrives, times gamma to whatever power the clocks call for. k is +1 if the answer is counted in the receiver's own ticks and -1 if the source is the one moving - a numerator reduction, since a slowed source pulses less often - and 0 in the lattice's own frame, which is where the dynamics run
γ = (1-β2)-1/2
premise budget/what-a-tick-is-spent-on
the clock advances by the crossing component, which is the root of that - so a moving thing ticks at sqrt(1 - β2) and one lattice tick is worth (1 - β2)-1/2 of its own. The Lorentz factor, out of a step of fixed length and nothing else
γ = (1-β2)-1/2
by kept exact
γ is (1-β2) to the -1/2, and it is carried as that rather than expanded. The exponent is not a whole positive number, so a series would be infinite and would have to be cut somewhere - and anything built on the cut version inherits the cut. Kept closed it is exact
Fgrel = Fg·retardation(1-β2)(mr-ms)/2
by substituting
γ is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1(1-β2)1/2, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
Fg = Fmeet + Fvac
premise definition:gravity.full
what a body feels is everything that arrives at it, and things that arrive add. So the gravitational force is the two channels together: the meetings between the bodies' own radiation, and the expansion the vacuum did not manage around them
Fvac = A⊥ · SSTEP·R-D+1
premise definition:gravity.full
and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part
Fg = A⊥·SRD-1·STEP + Fmeet
by substituting
Fvac is not a primitive of this theory - it is A⊥·SRD-1·STEP, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
S = blocked · expansion
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
each blocked cell is one point that would have expanded and did not, so the shortfall is how many are blocked times how fast each would have grown. THIS IS GRAVITY IN THIS MODEL: not a pull between bodies but an expansion that did not happen, spreading outward from whatever was in the way. A second body is pushed toward it because fewer rays arrive from that direction than from the far side
blocked = A'
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
the split fails to fire at every cell the body owns, so the suppression itself goes as its volume - but a shortfall deep inside is filled in by its neighbours before it gets out. What reaches the medium beyond has to cross the boundary, and how many ways there are through it is the body's area. So what a distant body feels is limited by the surface, and a bigger surface pulls harder
S = A'·expansion
by substituting
blocked is not a primitive of this theory - it is A', so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
expansion = 1
premise definition:vacuum.expansion
the split fires on a point because the point is NEUTRAL, and it does not ask what this theory's rays carry - so every neutral point makes one point every tick, in every theory here. That is the rate space is made at, and it is the same number whatever is running
S = A'
by substituting
expansion is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

by substituting
S is not a primitive of this theory - it is A', so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

retardation = w·ahead + (1-w)·behind
premise definition:gravity.relativistic
how much of the time you are on each side is w and 1 - w, so what arrives is the two branches at those weights. Ignorance is w = 1/2 and is not a special case of anything - it is the value that makes the two equal. What this average COMES to is not stated here: it is put over a common denominator by the rules below, and what falls out is exact
w = 1 + cos(θ)2
premise definition:gravity.relativistic
the share of the motion lying along the line between the two bodies is (1 + cos θ)/2 - one when the source comes straight at you, nought when it goes straight away, a half across. This is geometry and not belief, and writing it as a state of knowledge made a fact about angles look like a fact about the observer
retardation = 1/2·ahead + 1/2·ahead·cos(θ) + 1/2·behind - 1/2·behind·cos(θ)
by substituting
w is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1/2 + 1/2·cos(θ), so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
ahead = 1 + v
premise definition:matter.wavelength
the branch that set out ahead of the source is compressed by its motion - the retarded time carries a 1/(1 - v), which to first order in a small speed is 1 + v
retardation = 1/2 + 1/2·behind - 1/2·behind·cos(θ) + 1/2·cos(θ) + 1/2·cos(θ)·v + 1/2·v
by substituting
ahead is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 + v, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
behind = 1 - v
premise definition:matter.wavelength
the branch behind is stretched by the same motion by the same amount the other way - 1/(1 + v), which to first order is 1 - v
retardation = 1 + cos(θ)·v
by substituting
behind is not a primitive of this theory - it is 1 - v, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out

Fmeet = lean · share · SHEET2 · ma · mb · met(R)
premise definition:gravity.full
what arrives through MEETINGS is what a meeting is worth to a path, times how much of the time the two phases are opposed, times the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, times the two masses, times the meetings summed along the line between them. Every one of those was proved somewhere else and is cited; this line only says how they multiply
lean = cDEG
premise definition:lattice.lean
an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, while every other way out of that point still weighs exactly what it did before - and there are DEG of those. So the lean is a step against DEG: what the annihilation bought, over the alternatives it did not take. The numerator is c rather than a bare 1 because what it bought is a step, and a step is c
c = 1
premise counts/what-the-tiling-fixes
a step's worth of lean is what one annihilation buys a path, and a step is c - one cell a tick, the lattice's own speed. Its value in those units is one, which is a statement about the units and not about the quantity. A count of the tiling, taken off the geometry itself with nothing run and nothing fitted
c = 1
by a number is an expression
c is 1, so it can stand in an expression as that
DEG = 12

share = annihilatingcases
premise definition:share.coherence
two charges are opposed exactly when their meeting leaves nothing - that is what the word means for a rule that either annihilates a pair or does not. The states a pair can be in are equally available, so how much of the time they are opposed is how many of those states annihilate, over how many there are
annihilating = 1

and left nothing at all in the other 1: those are the states in which the two were opposed, which is what being opposed MEANS in a theory whose meetings either annihilate a pair or do not

met(R) = metfar·(1 + near)
premise definition:met.integral
so the whole of it is the long-range law times one plus a correction. The one is what becomes Newton's inverse square; the correction is the middle's logarithm over the long-range term, and it carries c/R - worth per cent at a few cells and nothing at all once R is an astronomical number of lattice steps
near = the middlemetfar
premise definition:met.integral
the correction is what the middle's tail is worth against the long-range law - a ratio of the two, and the thing that goes to nothing as R grows
near = the middlemetfar
by as a ratio
near is the middle over metfar, which written out is the middlemetfar - kept in the counts rather than worked out, so that whatever uses it can cancel against them
met(R) = metfar + the middle
by substituting
near is not a primitive of this theory - it is the middlemetfar, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
the middle = ∫Rc the middle's tail dx
premise definition:met.integral
the middle runs from the edge of one core to the edge of the other, and one over x integrated between them is a logarithm - which grows more slowly than any power, and is the whole of why the correction dies away
the middle's tail = R-D·1x
premise definition:met.integral
between the two cores the integrand is a genuine product of two falling densities. By partial fractions that splits into a part carrying the same power of the separation as the cores do - which sums with them - and this part, one power of R further down and going as one over the distance along the line. It is the second that gives the correction, and being a power lower is exactly why the correction shrinks as the bodies are moved apart
the middle = ln(R/c)RD
by integrating a power
the middle's tail goes as one over x, whose integral is a logarithm - so between c and R it is ln(R/c). It grows more slowly than any power of x, which is what matters about it here
met(R) = metfar + ln(R/c)RD

one core = ∫c0 the integrand in a core dx
premise definition:met.integral
one core runs from the body out to a distance of one core, and across it the integrand is flat - so its contribution is that value times the width
the integrand in a core = c-D+1·R-D+1
premise definition:met.integral
inside the core at one end the near density has flattened off at its cap - a shell is never smaller than the cell its source sits in - while the far density barely moves across a width of one core. So the integrand there is the product of the two, neither depending on x any more. How fast each thins is the dense regime's: there are partners everywhere, so the hand-off is never what a carrier waits for and the lattice's one-cell-a-tick is the binding bound

what survives = expansion · occupancy
premise definition:vacuum.expansion
how much of what was made is still there once the two halves have met is a different question, and its answer is the occupancy - enumerated from the meeting rule rather than measured. Pure gravity makes space at the same rate as anything else and keeps none of it; a theory whose rays carry a sign keeps half. What matter is in the way of is the MAKING, which is why gravity works in both

Fmeet = lean · share · SHEET2 · ma · mb · met(R)
premise definition:gravity.full
what arrives through MEETINGS is what a meeting is worth to a path, times how much of the time the two phases are opposed, times the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, times the two masses, times the meetings summed along the line between them. Every one of those was proved somewhere else and is cited; this line only says how they multiply
share = annihilatingcases
premise definition:share.coherence
two charges are opposed exactly when their meeting leaves nothing - that is what the word means for a rule that either annihilates a pair or does not. The states a pair can be in are equally available, so how much of the time they are opposed is how many of those states annihilate, over how many there are

met(R) = metfar·(1 + near)
premise definition:met.integral
so the whole of it is the long-range law times one plus a correction. The one is what becomes Newton's inverse square; the correction is the middle's logarithm over the long-range term, and it carries c/R - worth per cent at a few cells and nothing at all once R is an astronomical number of lattice steps

near = the middlemetfar

the middle = ∫Rc the middle's tail dx
premise definition:met.integral
the middle runs from the edge of one core to the edge of the other, and one over x integrated between them is a logarithm - which grows more slowly than any power, and is the whole of why the correction dies away
the middle's tail = R-D·1x
premise definition:met.integral
between the two cores the integrand is a genuine product of two falling densities. By partial fractions that splits into a part carrying the same power of the separation as the cores do - which sums with them - and this part, one power of R further down and going as one over the distance along the line. It is the second that gives the correction, and being a power lower is exactly why the correction shrinks as the bodies are moved apart
the middle = ln(R/c)RD
by integrating a power
the middle's tail goes as one over x, whose integral is a logarithm - so between c and R it is ln(R/c). It grows more slowly than any power of x, which is what matters about it here

the derivation, 40 steps
Fg = Fmeet + Fvac
premise definition:gravity.full
what a body feels is everything that arrives at it, and things that arrive add. So the gravitational force is the two channels together: the meetings between the bodies' own radiation, and the expansion the vacuum did not manage around them
Fvac = A⊥ · SSTEP·R-D+1
premise definition:gravity.full
and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part
Fg = A⊥·SRD-1·STEP + Fmeet

Fvac is not a primitive of this theory - it is A⊥·SRD-1·STEP, so it stands in for itself here and the result is multiplied out
S = blocked · expansion
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
each blocked cell is one point that would have expanded and did not, so the shortfall is how many are blocked times how fast each would have grown. THIS IS GRAVITY IN THIS MODEL: not a pull between bodies but an expansion that did not happen, spreading outward from whatever was in the way. A second body is pushed toward it because fewer rays arrive from that direction than from the far side
blocked = A'
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
the split fails to fire at every cell the body owns, so the suppression itself goes as its volume - but a shortfall deep inside is filled in by its neighbours before it gets out. What reaches the medium beyond has to cross the boundary, and how many ways there are through it is the body's area. So what a distant body feels is limited by the surface, and a bigger surface pulls harder

expansion = 1
premise definition:vacuum.expansion
the split fires on a point because the point is NEUTRAL, and it does not ask what this theory's rays carry - so every neutral point makes one point every tick, in every theory here. That is the rate space is made at, and it is the same number whatever is running

Fmeet = lean · share · SHEET2 · ma · mb · met(R)
premise definition:gravity.full
what arrives through MEETINGS is what a meeting is worth to a path, times how much of the time the two phases are opposed, times the charges each pulse lets go on both sides, times the two masses, times the meetings summed along the line between them. Every one of those was proved somewhere else and is cited; this line only says how they multiply
lean = cDEG
premise definition:lattice.lean
an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, while every other way out of that point still weighs exactly what it did before - and there are DEG of those. So the lean is a step against DEG: what the annihilation bought, over the alternatives it did not take. The numerator is c rather than a bare 1 because what it bought is a step, and a step is c
c = 1
premise counts/what-the-tiling-fixes
a step's worth of lean is what one annihilation buys a path, and a step is c - one cell a tick, the lattice's own speed. Its value in those units is one, which is a statement about the units and not about the quantity. A count of the tiling, taken off the geometry itself with nothing run and nothing fitted

the middle's tail = R-D·1x
premise definition:met.integral
between the two cores the integrand is a genuine product of two falling densities. Fvac = A⊥ · SSTEP·R-D+1
premise definition:gravity.full
and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part
S = blocked · expansion
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
each blocked cell is one point that would have expanded and did not, so the shortfall is how many are blocked times how fast each would have grown. THIS IS GRAVITY IN THIS MODEL: not a pull between bodies but an expansion that did not happen, spreading outward from whatever was in the way. A second body is pushed toward it because fewer rays arrive from that direction than from the far side
blocked = A'
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
the split fails to fire at every cell the body owns, so the suppression itself goes as its volume - but a shortfall deep inside is filled in by its neighbours before it gets out. What reaches the medium beyond has to cross the boundary, and how many ways there are through it is the body's area. So what a distant body feels is limited by the surface, and a bigger surface pulls harder

premise turning/is-a-turn-a-rotation
the exits' second moment comes to 4.000000, which is DEG/D = 12/3 exactly, and the tensor is isotropic to 7.8e-16. The exits are manifestly NOT an isotropic set - they point at particular neighbours - and their second moment is isotropic anyway, the tiling's symmetry being enough. So no lattice anisotropy leaks into the force and the law reads the same in every orientation. This is a count of the tiling, not a fitted coupling, and it is a check that could have failed

the derivation, 8 steps
what a ray carries as polarity is conserved in flight
premise carried/what-a-ray-keeps
run with MOVEMENT and ARRIVAL and nothing else, the multiset of what the rays are carrying as polarity is exactly what it was 6 ticks earlier. Transport writes each ray's contents onto one neighbour and swaps them in, and polarity is part of what a ray carries - so it is moved and neither made nor unmade. Compared as a MULTISET rather than as a sum, so a rule that swapped two rays' labels would be caught rather than counted as conservative. This holds at every shell at once and for every run length, because it is a property of the rule. Set aside to ask it: EMISSION, CREATION, ANNIHILATION, TRANSPORT
what a ray carries as polarity goes every way alike
premise carried/what-a-ray-keeps
handed a source with no axis, GXOR's own EMISSION rule wrote the same value of polarity on every one of its 6 exits - not most of them, all of them. So what a round source puts out goes every way alike, which is what says a share is the whole of it over the WHOLE shell rather than over some part of it
n[what a ray carries as polarity] ∝ what a ray carries as polarityshell
by spreading
conserved and even, so one site's share is the whole of it over the number of sites there are at that distance
shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 3, which is D, exactly and on integers
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
by Ehrhart's theorem
Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1

the same argument, over a different amount of room. deficit is conserved on its way out and goes every way alike, so one site's share is the whole of it over however many sites there are at that distance - and how many that is depends on the shape of what it came from. Here that is shell about a 0-dimensional source rather than the shell about a point, and nothing else in the argument changes
ball about a 0-dimensional source(r) = |r·P⊥ ∩ L|
premise extent/room-around-a-source-of-any-size
the sites within r steps of a source spanning 0 directions are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step of it, in the 3 directions ACROSS it - the source already spans the other 0, so nothing grows that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 3, which is D-0, exactly and on integers
ball about a 0-dimensional source(r) ∝ STEP·rD
by Ehrhart's theorem
Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality
shell about a 0-dimensional source(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
by the difference of a dilate
every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1
n[deficit] per shell about a 0-dimensional source ∝ SSTEP·rD-1
by expansion
shell about a 0-dimensional source is not a primitive of this theory - it is what the line above shows it to be, so it stands in for itself here
S = blocked · expansion
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
each blocked cell is one point that would have expanded and did not, so the shortfall is how many are blocked times how fast each would have grown. THIS IS GRAVITY IN THIS MODEL: not a pull between bodies but an expansion that did not happen, spreading outward from whatever was in the way. A second body is pushed toward it because fewer rays arrive from that direction than from the far side
S ∝ blocked·expansion
by which is also a scaling
S is blocked·expansion, which is a single product of powers - so it scales as that, and whatever was written in terms of S can be written in terms of what it is made of
blocked = A'
premise definition:vacuum.suppression
the split fails to fire at every cell the body owns, so the suppression itself goes as its volume - but a shortfall deep inside is filled in by its neighbours before it gets out. What reaches the medium beyond has to cross the boundary, and how many ways there are through it is the body's area. So what a distant body feels is limited by the surface, and a bigger surface pulls harder

the derivation, 16 steps
deficit is conserved in flight
premise medium/what-transport-does
run with MOVEMENT and ARRIVAL and nothing else, the number of rays in the world does not change: 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250. MOVEMENT writes each ray's contents onto exactly one neighbour and ARRIVAL makes that the ray, so transport is a bijection - it moves what it carries and neither makes nor unmakes any of it. This holds at every shell at once and for every run length, because it is a property of the rule rather than of a configuration. What was set aside to ask it: EMISSION, CREATION, ANNIHILATION, TRANSPORT - so this is what the medium does while CARRYING a disturbance, and anything those rules do to one is a correction on top of it
deficit travels through ρ
premise medium/what-transport-does
transport is the only rule that changes where anything is, and it moves along the lattice's own exits - one exit a tick, watched here as a front that never runs ahead of the steps it has taken. So a disturbance gets from here to there BY TRAVELLING THROUGH the medium, which is what makes the medium's own evenness a fact about the disturbance as well
the lattice carries alike in every direction
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
the exit set's second moment is a multiple of the identity, so nothing carried on this lattice prefers a direction at second order
deficit goes every way alike

deficit travels through ρ, and ρ prefers no direction - so neither does what it carries

retardation = w·ahead + (1-w)·behind
premise definition:gravity.relativistic
how much of the time you are on each side is w and 1 - w, so what arrives is the two branches at those weights. Ignorance is w = 1/2 and is not a special case of anything - it is the value that makes the two equal. What this average COMES to is not stated here: it is put over a common denominator by the rules below, and what falls out is exact
w = 1 + cos(θ)2
premise definition:gravity.relativistic
the share of the motion lying along the line between the two bodies is (1 + cos θ)/2 - one when the source comes straight at you, nought when it goes straight away, a half across. This is geometry and not belief, and writing it as a state of knowledge made a fact about angles look like a fact about the observer

premise medium/what-transport-does
run with MOVEMENT and ARRIVAL and nothing else, the number of rays in the world does not change: 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250, 1250. MOVEMENT writes each ray's contents onto exactly one neighbour and ARRIVAL makes that the ray, so transport is a bijection - it moves what it carries and neither makes nor unmakes any of it. This holds at every shell at once and for every run length, because it is a property of the rule rather than of a configuration. What was set aside to ask it: EMISSION, CREATION, ANNIHILATION, TRANSPORT - so this is what the medium does while CARRYING a disturbance, and anything those rules do to one is a correction on top of it
deficit travels through ρ
premise medium/what-transport-does
transport is the only rule that changes where anything is, and it moves along the lattice's own exits - one exit a tick, watched here as a front that never runs ahead of the steps it has taken. So a disturbance gets from here to there BY TRAVELLING THROUGH the medium, which is what makes the medium's own evenness a fact about the disturbance as well

shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)

ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 3, which is D, exactly and on integers
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
by Ehrhart's theorem
Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
by the difference of a dilate
every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

premise definition:gravity.full
and what arrives because the vacuum's expansion was SUPPRESSED is the other channel. A body's cells are not neutral, so the split does not fire on them; the expansion that did not happen there spreads outward and a second body is pushed into the shortfall. This needs neither body to emit anything - an inert absorber has it - which is what makes it a separate arrival rather than the meeting term counted again. It thins as the dense regime says, because the deficit is carried by the same rays as everything else. Note the two areas are not the same kind of area: what the near body SENDS leaves through the whole of its boundary and spreads isotropically, so its full A' counts; what the far body FEELS is an imbalance along the line between them, so only its facing cross-section takes part

by Ehrhart's theorem
Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. shell(r) = ball(r) - ball(r-1)
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
a site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the sites at exactly r steps are those within r less those within r-1 - a subtraction, with nothing left over and nothing counted twice
ball(r) = |r·P ∩ L|
premise lattice/what-the-tiling-is
the sites within r steps are the r-fold dilate of the sites within one step - take one step r times and you are somewhere in r·P, and every site of r·P is reached that way. Checked: the counts walked out of the lattice are a polynomial in r of degree 3, which is D, exactly and on integers
ball(r) ∝ STEP·rD
by Ehrhart's theorem
Ehrhart 1962: the number of lattice points in the k-fold dilate of a lattice polytope is a polynomial in k of degree exactly D, whose leading coefficient is the polytope's volume. Here k is r and P is the set of sites one step from the centre, so the ball's count is a polynomial in r of degree D and everything below the leading term is dropped by the proportionality
shell(r) ∝ STEP·rD-1
by the difference of a dilate
every site is either within r-1 steps or it is not, so the shell is the ball less its own shift by one step. Expanding (r-1)D by the binomial theorem, the leading β·rD cancels against the ball's, and what survives is D·β·rD-1. The D came DOWN from the exponent in that cancellation; a proportionality does not carry it, and the exponent left behind is D-1

what the corpus holds

A candidate is called novel when it matches nothing in 81 laws written in this same vocabulary - gravitation, electromagnetism, mechanics, relativity, quantum, waves, thermal, cosmology, geometry, dimensionless. That is a claim about the corpus as much as about the candidate.

what is still being taken on trust

Every one of these is a line some theorem writes down as a definition, turned round and stated as an experiment. They are ordered by how much is waiting on them, which is the only ordering that matters when the list is a work queue - and the top of it is usually not where you would have looked.

the two ways a symbol is matched

A candidate is compared with the corpus after this model's own counts are divided out and its symbols are put into the corpus's names. Renaming is free - the same quantity, two spellings. Reading is not: it is a claim of this model's, and any match that needed one says so on the row.

Sm a reading, untested - the expansion the near body's boundary SUPPRESSED - an amount of space per tick that did not get made, which is what the glossary says it is and which is a quantity about space rather than about matter. Reading it as mass is not a category error, it is this model's central identification: the extra gravity IS the expansion being blocked, so how much a body blocks is what its mass amounts to. But it is an identification, so it has to be measured. MARKED REFUTED HERE ON EVIDENCE THAT WAS NOT ABOUT IT. The run attached to this row measured the body's caught-count - rays it absorbed - across four duty cycles, which is not the suppressed expansion and never was. S is what did NOT get made near the body, so what would settle it is counting the splits that failed to happen against an identical world with no body in it. Until that is run this row says nothing either way
A'm a reading, refuted - the ways across a body's boundary, read as its mass. the same runs counted the exits leading out of the body's own cells: 60 at every duty cycle. A boundary is fixed by the body's radius
A⊥m' a reading, refuted - the part of the far body's boundary that faces the line, read as the far body's mass. a facing cross-section is a fixed fraction of the boundary, and the boundary does not move with the duty cycle - 60 ways at all four
Am' a reading, refuted - the whole of a body's boundary, read as its mass. 60 ways across it at every duty cycle
n[what a ray carries as polarity]E a reading, untested - the density of net polarity the medium is left holding, read as the electric field itself. The article states this outright - the net polarity a charge leaves in the vacuum IS the field, read directly rather than differentiated out of a potential - which makes it exactly the kind of claim that has to be measured rather than adopted. Nothing has yet asked a run whether a test charge placed in that density feels what the field says it should
what a ray carries as polarityq a reading, untested - the signed thing a ray carries, read as electric charge. Transport conserves it exactly and a round source puts out a net of it while an axial source puts out none - which is everything a charge is asked to do, and still not a measurement that it IS one
δpotential a reading, untested - the disturbance left in the medium, read as a potential
deficitpotential a reading, untested - the shortfall a body leaves, read as a potential

what this vocabulary cannot say

For anything on this list, "matches nothing" means the corpus cannot hold the law, not that the law is unknown.

  • Maxwell's equations as equations - they relate fields to their own derivatives across space and time; this vocabulary has scalings and products, not differential operators. What survives here is their falloff skeleton - the r^-2, the r^-3 and the r^-1
  • anything with a tensor in it - general relativity's field equations, stress and strain, the metric as an object - a Fact is about a scalar quantity. A metric COMPONENT can appear; the metric cannot
  • gauge structure and conservation as a consequence of symmetry - conservation is a premise here, not something derived from an invariance - there is no group in this vocabulary and so no Noether argument
  • variational principles - least action, Lagrangians, Hamiltonians - these are statements about a functional over paths; nothing here quantifies over paths
  • operator ordering, commutators, entanglement - quantities here are numbers that multiply commutatively. The scaling shadows of quantum mechanics are in the corpus; its algebra is not
  • anything exponential - Boltzmann factors, tunnelling, radioactive decay - `raised` carries a rational power of a base, not a base raised to a variable
  • phase transitions and critical exponents as a class - expressible one at a time as scalings, but the renormalisation argument that explains why they are universal is not
